headline: CENTINELA COPPER STRIKE ESCALATES: THREE WORKERS START HUNGER PROTEST — LME COPPER SETTLES AT $14,540
snippet: Three union leaders at Antofagasta's Centinela copper mine in northern Chile escalated a strike that began October 7 by starting a hunger protest on October 9, as mediation between 709 workers and management remained deadlocked over pay equity with a third union. BMO Capital Markets flagged that while processing plants can continue operating near-term, a prolonged stoppage could reduce copper production by up to 50% in November. Antofagasta maintains its full-year production guidance, but traders are watching closely: LME copper rose 1.6% on Friday to settle at $14,540 per tonne, recording a 2% weekly gain driven by combined Chile supply fears and Chinese restocking signals ahead of the post-Golden Week return.

headline: SILVER SURGES 2% FRIDAY TO $60.84 AS GOLD/SILVER RATIO COMPRESSES TO 69.36
snippet: Silver gained 2.04% on October 9 to settle at $60.84 per troy ounce, outperforming gold's 1.31% gain on the same day and compressing the gold/silver ratio to 69.36 — a level that marks improving relative performance for the industrial-precious metal after a month of underperformance. The precious metals complex recovered from a mid-week dip triggered by energy inflation data that briefly revived Federal Reserve rate-hike speculation. Despite a 4.79% monthly decline, silver remains 20.33% above year-ago levels; bulls point to the metal's ability to hold above the $60 psychological floor as evidence the October correction is technical rather than a fundamental reversal.

headline: LITHIUM CARBONATE FALLS TO 122,350 CNY/T ON OCT 9 — SEPTEMBER'S 22.5% CRASH DEEPENS
snippet: Battery-grade lithium carbonate fell an additional 2.08% on October 9 to 122,350 yuan per tonne on the Guangzhou futures exchange, extending a September collapse that wiped 22.5% off the commodity from its May 2026 two-year high near 158,000 yuan/t. The metal remains approximately 66% above year-ago levels but is down 15.48% over the past month, raising concerns about oversupply entering the traditionally stronger Q4 battery procurement season. Junior lithium miners on the TSX-V and ASX that built market-cap narratives around the May breakout face mounting NAV mark-to-market pressure if the trend continues through year-end.

headline: SIGMA LITHIUM RESTARTS GROTA DO CIRILO AFTER BRAZIL APPEALS COURT REVERSES MINE SHUTDOWN
snippet: Sigma Lithium (TSX: SGML) resumed mining and processing at its Grota do Cirilo complex in Minas Gerais state on October 7 after a Brazilian federal appeals court reversed an emergency suspension order that had idled the facility for weeks. The court upheld Sigma's environmental licences in a suit brought by the Quilombola community association Ngolo over a disputed perimeter boundary. The company maintained its annualized lithium oxide concentrate production target of 330,000 tonnes by end-2027 while shifting its rolling 12-month guidance window by approximately three months to reflect the suspension period — a positive resolution that removes the legal overhang investors had been pricing into the stock.

headline: URANIUM SPOT HOLDS AT $89.85/LB AS LONG-TERM CONTRACT PRICES NEAR $97 ON DATA CENTER DEMAND
snippet: Uranium spot prices held at $89.85 per pound through October 8 while the long-term contract market approached $97 per pound — a spread of approximately $7 that reflects sustained utility buying driven by electricity demand growth from data centers, AI infrastructure, and EVs. The widening gap between spot and term prices signals utilities are paying a premium for supply certainty, a pattern that historically precedes spot price convergence upward. Australian uranium miners separately rallied this week after Google announced a power purchase agreement with Constellation Energy, reinforcing the narrative that the energy transition is actively expanding the addressable uranium demand base.

headline: NASDAQ SPAC MERGES WITH TITAN STRATEGICS IN $318M URANIUM DEAL TARGETING SWEDISH BILLINGEN DISTRICT
snippet: Digital Asset Acquisition Corp. (Nasdaq: DAAQ) filed a merger agreement with Titan Strategics Holdings Ltd, a Cayman Islands company whose subsidiary holds the exploration licence over the former Ranstad uranium mine and surrounding Billingen uranium district in Sweden. The combined entity will be renamed Renaissance Nuclear, Inc. upon closing, which is subject to shareholder and regulatory approvals; the implied pro-forma enterprise value is approximately $318 million. The deal adds a Nordic uranium developer to the market's pipeline at a moment when spot prices hold near $89.85/lb and long-term contracts trade toward $97/lb — Swedish uranium assets carry a tier-1 jurisdiction premium that is increasingly relevant as utilities review supply diversification.

headline: USA RARE EARTH SLIDES 4.5% FOR SECOND STRAIGHT DAY — CRITICAL METALS SECTOR BUILDERS HIT HARDER THAN PRODUCERS
snippet: USA Rare Earth (Nasdaq: USAR) fell approximately 4.5% on October 9 in the second consecutive session of heavy sector selling, following a 5% decline on October 8, with United States Antimony dropping roughly 4% and the VanEck Rare Earth and Strategic Metals ETF shedding about 3%. The selloff has erased approximately 28% of USAR's value over the past month despite the company finalizing US$1.6 billion in Commerce Department funding for its Texas mine-to-magnet build-out in June 2026. Analysts say the divergence between builders and producers is driven by execution timeline risk: established producers like MP Materials (~$8.6B market cap) are holding better than pre-revenue companies still years from first output, reinforcing the case for rigorous due diligence on milestone risk.

headline: ANGLO AMERICAN CEO: MINING M&A IN 'NEW WATERS' AS CHINA REMAINS LAST HURDLE FOR TECK MERGER
snippet: Anglo American CEO Duncan Wanblad said on October 7 that global mining dealmaking has entered 'new waters,' citing geopolitical complexity as the dominant factor shaping M&A outcomes for the sector. The roughly US$54 billion Anglo American–Teck Resources merger has received all required approvals except China, with closing now expected by March 2027. Simultaneously, the European Commission issued a statement of objections to Anglo's proposed sale of its Brazil nickel assets to MMG — with MMG pushing back, calling the allegations a conspiracy theory. The dual-track process illustrates how large critical minerals deals spanning multiple jurisdictions require managing competing national interests, a structural shift that junior mining investors should factor into deal timing and valuation assumptions.

headline: TOP 50 MINING COMPANIES SHED $264 BILLION IN Q3 AS GOLD RETREATS FROM PEAK AND LITHIUM STOCKS EXIT
snippet: A Mining.com analysis of the 50 largest mining companies by market capitalization found the cohort shed approximately $264 billion in collective value during Q3 2026 as gold retreated from its January all-time high near $5,600 per ounce and institutional investors rotated out of lithium-exposed names following the commodity's sharp pullback. The magnitude of the decline underscores the leverage — both positive and negative — that commodity price movements exert on mining equity market caps at scale. For retail investors holding junior positions, the data is a structural reminder: small-cap mining stocks amplify these moves significantly, and a 22% gold pullback from peak can produce 40-60% declines in explorers with no near-term cash flow.

headline: GOLD MINERS BEGIN Q4 ON WEAK FOOTING AFTER RECORD Q3 RUN — ANALYSTS SPLIT ON WHAT'S NEXT
snippet: A new Seeking Alpha analysis examines which gold mining equities have preserved value after the NYSE Arca Gold Miners Index's 17.4% Q3 run, finding the sector started Q4 on a weak note following September's commodity price retreat. The piece identifies royalty and streaming names plus low-cost producers as the relative winners, while development-stage and single-commodity explorers with execution issues have given back proportionally more. Analysts are split: bulls cite the GDX's demonstrated ability to outperform the S&P 500 by 7.5x over the full quarter as evidence the secular trend remains intact, while cautious voices flag that more volatility is likely near the $4,200 gold support zone before a sustainable Q4 recovery takes hold.

headline: UBS PICKS PREFERRED GOLD MINING STOCKS FOR 2027 AS SECTOR FACES RISING COST PRESSURES
snippet: UBS analysts named preferred gold mining stocks in a research note acknowledging the sector is heading into rising cost pressure in 2027 even as the long-term gold price outlook remains constructive after January 2026's all-time high near $5,400. With gold having retreated roughly 22% from its peak to the current $4,187-$4,202 range, UBS frames the current environment as a stock-selection trade rather than a broad sector allocation — favouring royalty and streaming names and disciplined low-cost producers over development-stage plays exposed to labour and energy cost inflation. Agnico Eagle and Franco-Nevada were among the names highlighted as preferred holdings heading into a seasonally active Q4 contracting and capital-allocation period.
